cells.tense: You can look a thing through and let it go while your hand is still open.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: Take a knot you keep circling and write out only what actually follows from it, in a few plain lines. Then stop there. Nothing else needs writing down.
cells.core:
You can stay with something until it is fully in view, and part of that is knowing when the picture is done, which is what lets you set it down instead of carrying it around half-lit. Most people can't stop looking. You can.

The step available now is to work a knot through to its logic rather than finding one more angle on it. Write what follows from it in plain lines, then stop. What brought you here was letting go with your hand open, and the picture doesn't have to stay unfinished to be true. A finished look is easier to carry than a half-one and easier to put down.

cells.tense: You will have it understood whole before it has finished happening to you.
cells.act: let the impulse start without a plan
cells.ask: Let one impulse this week start without a plan — no name on it, no outcome picked. Begin it and keep it undecided for a single day.
cells.core:
Where you look, the conclusion lands before the middle has occurred. Somebody starts a sentence and you have the end of it. A thing turns and you've decided how it turns out. Nothing wrong with how you see — it runs early, before the moment it's about, so nothing gets to arrive unclaimed. Even what would be better left open gets read on the way in. A person who shines because they see, and not to get there first, carries it differently.

What's open to you is a start that isn't pointed anywhere yet. Next time something begins, catch it before you name a direction and keep it undecided an hour, a day. You'll still see it. You just won't finish a thing that hasn't got going.

cells.tense: A full way of looking is in you, and right now it is not running.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Put something you might build next into a single line: just what it is, nothing more. Keep that line where you can find it, and spend nothing on it yet.
cells.core:
You catch the first edge of something and stop there. What's here now arrives and the room feels occupied already, so it doesn't get looked at all the way through. This is not a small strength in you. It sits unused while something else takes the attention.

Looking harder won't revive it. Give it one object to hold. Take whatever you might make next and put it in a single line — what it is, not the shape of the plan. Write it where you can find it, and leave it there until it grows past a single line. That is enough to bring the rest of you forward, and it asks for nothing you don't already hold.

cells.tense: You notice things clearly all day and tell it as though it happened to somebody else.
cells.act: take the turning as it comes
cells.ask: Once this week, take a turning as it comes rather than as the next step in a run. Nothing to announce. Just be present when it arrives.
cells.core:
Things get clear where you are, a situation lightens, a hand lets go — and the story you tell is that it cleared by itself, or that anyone standing there would have picked up on it. Either may be true. It's also true that nobody wrote your name on it, which is a strange place to keep the thing you're best at.

There's a simpler spot to stand. Something is entering now, and it arrives to find you meeting it — not the aftermath, this. Once this week, take a turning as it comes rather than the next step in a run of them, and let it be yours that you were present for it. No announcement. Just the plain fact that you were there.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that the person's seeing is complete or total — the record names that state, but at Balanced I can only say the capacity is working, not that anything is finished. The reader could reasonably say nothing feels complete and that I'm describing someone else. The asks survive being wrong — skipping one move, writing the facts, waiting a day, meeting what arrives are all useful even if the read is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying they have already seen everything; it flatters the reading at their expense, so I've kept the seeing as something they do with what's in hand.
